title: Week 2 Tutorials — Importing Camera Footage & Multi-Camera Editing in Premiere Pro
description:
This tutorials help you navigate camera imports using a USB cable in both Mac (using the Photos App) and Windows, while Premiere Pro tutorials will help you navigate multi-camera editing.

Adobe Premiere Pro is a professional video editing software used to assemble, sequence, and export time-based media. In industry, it is commonly used for film, television, online video, and experimental media production, supporting workflows that combine image, sound, and timing.

description: These tutorials builds on Week 1 by introducing workflows specific to interview-based and multi-camera editing. Students will learn how to import footage directly from a camera (via SD card or USB), organize clips from multiple cameras, synchronize audio and video using clap sync, and sequence three camera angles within the timeline. The tutorials also cover basic cropping and trimming for pacing, as well as an introduction to multi-camera editing techniques suitable for documentary interviews.

children.title: HOW TO ORGANIZE YOUR PREMIERE PROJECT - Premiere Pro Organization - Filmmaking 101
children.description: In this video, your will learn how to organize your Adobe Premiere project so that you can be more streamlined and work faster. Premiere Pro organization is super-important, especially if you are going to be handing your project off to another editor at some point.

children.title: How to sync multiple clips in premiere - Fast editor pro tip
children.description: Learn how to sync multiple clips in premiere by audio. The method you should be using is presented in the first 30 seconds. The rest of the video is useful if you have multiple different shots of the same or several interviews.

children.title: How to Edit 2 Camera Interviews Like a Pro (Advance)
children.description: Here's how to edit multi-camera interviews in Adobe Premiere, and incorporate b-roll, graphics, and music. Knowing how to sync and create sequences from 2 cameras (or more) is a crucial skill for professional assistant editors and editors.
